scope: Selected adapted briefs and teaching guides, with completion stated per component. Not a complete exam paper, official marking scheme or timed-paper simulation.

components.subject: Mathematics
components.selection: Question 6 parts (a)–(d): graph scales, quadratic coefficients, line gradient and positive interval
components.coverage: 4 of 4 selected parts in one adapted guide with an original in-page graph
components.review: Official prompt and examiner images freshly fetched and visually inspected 2026-09-28. Independent checks of roots -2 and 4, ordinate 8, P(-5,-27), Q(3,5) give coefficients (-1,2,8), line gradient 4 and positive interval -2<x<4, agreeing with the examiner solution. Original redraw uses equal major squares for 2 x-units and 10 y-units, with the source paper's 2 cm convention stated separately from responsive screen dimensions. Plotted data have a localized text alternative; solved formulas remain in the optional worked answer. No WAEC image is hosted.

components.subject: Mathematics
components.selection: Question 8 parts (a)–(c): savings percentage, pie chart and after-tax monthly amounts
components.coverage: 3 of 3 selected parts across 2 adapted guides
components.review: The official WAEC question page supplies the budget table and all three parts. Its linked worked image shows 15% savings, sector angles 126°, 27°, 36°, 54°, 63° and 54°, monthly tax $288, and 15% of monthly after-tax pay $2,112 giving $316.80 savings. Each result was recalculated independently. AfroTools uses adapted briefs and does not reproduce the official chart or claim a complete paper.

components.review: WAEC's official 2021 WASSCE school-candidate Paper 2 pages display both Question 1 parts, all Question 11 frequency values, and the requested rounding. Student briefs are paraphrased and retain the calculation assumptions without republishing the paper.

components.review: The official 2021 Paper 2 Q5 and Q6 prompt and worked images were visually checked on 2026-09-27. Q5(a) shares 5%, 15%, 10%, 45%, 25% give 18°, 54°, 36°, 162°, 90°; Q5(b) five red of twelve without replacement gives 5/33. Q6(a) 80 students, 3/4 Biology and 3/5 Physics gives 28 in both and 2/5 Biology-only; Q6(b) 15 m × 8 m at GH¢890/m² gives GH¢106,800 carpeting and GH¢109,320 painting from GH¢216,120 total. Every result was independently recalculated. Adjacent Question 4 remains held because its official prompt and working images do not render.

components.subject: English
components.coverage: 5 of 5 composition choices; comprehension and summary are outside this selection
components.shared_rubric_review: WAEC's examiner pages identify the school-candidate paper and all five composition tasks but do not display the common Section A instruction or word limit. A secondary 2022 paper transcription says to answer one choice in at least 450 words. This is not authenticated as an official WAEC instruction and is not enforced by the companion.
components.review: Each question and examiner observation was inspected on WAEC's official site. The five independent briefs preserve audience, form and required parts without reproducing the prompts. Guidance addresses the observed mistakes: missing national benefit, confusing fake with hard drugs, listing improvements, using letter form for a speech, and a story without a relevant plot. No official marking scheme or automatic grade is claimed.

components.subject: English
components.session: WASSCE school candidates as identified by the WAEC examiner page; linked passage transcription is third-party
components.selection: Question 6 Section B comprehension teaching guide
components.coverage: One source-linked guide covering parts (a)–(h); passage and exact question text are not hosted
components.review: WAEC's official 2022 examiner page identifies Question 6 as comprehension and comments on grammar and vocabulary, but omits the passage, exact questions and answers. Studyzone and WikiQuestions transcriptions agree on the Alani passage and parts (a)–(h); Myschool corroborates the passage events. Each suggested answer was checked against the full passage and the clause and vocabulary in context. The WAEC observation calls the grammar item 6e, while the matching transcriptions place it at 6g; this unresolved numbering discrepancy does not support an official-answer claim. A matching original scan and permission to host the passage have not been established.

answer_review.basis: The opening account connects Alani's school performance with his teachers' regard.
The account of his new firm names hard work and a substantial investment of money and time as distinct causes of its success.
His arrogance, refusal to hear staff and poor treatment of clients precede the loss of clients and falling profits.
The same sequence makes his own conduct, rather than his workers, responsible for the decline he blamed on them.
Five workers leaving on the same day precedes his decision to seek counselling and change.
The firm is losing clients and profit when the idiom appears, supporting serious business difficulty.
The clause beginning with who supplies information about the noun phrase Alani's secretary.
Six replacements were checked in their sentence contexts: school awards, childhood food, the accounting firm's standing, the new enterprise, the owner's arrogance and falling profits.

components.rights_basis: Link to the third-party transcription and publish original paraphrased guidance only; no claim of permission to republish the passage or question text.
